body.en: It's midday, around 38°C, and you've been laying blocks outside for three hours without a break. You feel dizzy and your mouth is dry. What do you do?

choices.label: Stop now, move to shade, drink water, and rest until you feel normal again
choices.consequence: Right call. Dizziness and dry mouth in heat are early heat-exhaustion signs. Stopping, cooling down, and rehydrating now prevents it becoming heat stroke, which can be life-threatening.

choices.label: Push through — you're almost done for the day
choices.consequence: Risky. Ignoring early heat-exhaustion symptoms is exactly how heat stroke happens. The work will still be there after a 20-minute rest in the shade.

choices.label: Drink a cold soda instead of water and keep working
choices.consequence: Not ideal. Sugary drinks rehydrate you more slowly than water and don't address the real problem — you need to stop and cool down, not just drink something cold.
